title: Define immutable scorecard and classifier revisions with safe migration
description: Scope: first-class Scorecard and Classifier identities, separately immutable revisions. A scorecard revision pins ordered classifier revision references plus shared request/provider configuration and optimization policies; learned runtime checkpoints are distinct from editable definition revisions. Any classifier change creates a classifier revision and a new affected scorecard revision; never mutate old snapshots. Runs pin scorecard revision; predictions, human feedback and metrics identify classifier definition revision and actual learned configuration fingerprint. Define membership removal, renaming, reorder and multiple scorecard reuse semantics. GraphQL exposes create/read/edit-as-new-revision, revision comparison and explicit active revision selection. SQLite migration must preserve old runs, labels, comments and source provenance, be idempotent and transactional. Acceptance: tests prove edit isolation, joint-request cache invalidation, atomic membership updates, old-run readability and restoration of an old scorecard without overwriting newer history. Audit existing scorecards.py/catalog implementation before extending it; do not equate run numbering with the entire version model.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implemented and tested independent immutable scorecard definitions, ordered pinned classifier revisions, idempotent legacy-run-edition migration, edit propagation across active containing scorecards, explicit definition activation, fingerprints and GraphQL query/mutation surface. Existing runs remain untouched. Full Python suite: 610 passing. Still open: pin newly created runs directly to definition revisions, reconcile definition activation versus run-edition activation semantics, and complete runtime provenance integration; not closing this issue.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Added pure directional definition comparison and scorecardDefinitionComparison GraphQL query resolving exact pinned classifier versions. Comparisons preserve member order, additions/removals, changed classifier revisions, names and shared setting changes; unset differs from explicit null. Read-only UI drawer compares active to inspected revision without activation or model calls. Browser verified Anthus v2 to v1 shows Cyberian Gallery removed, original question/classes/roles and no shared-setting changes. Definition differences explicitly are not performance evidence. Remaining runtime/migration acceptance and matched protected performance comparison are not claimed complete.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Shared definition settings now validate executable defaults before immutable publication. Cadence controls and selection policies flow into frozen new-run configuration; existing runs are unchanged after later settings revisions. Legacy run-definition registration now retains optimization and rubric cadences instead of dropping them. Existing mapped historical definitions remain immutable. Tests cover invalid-save atomicity, no provider construction at run creation, shared policy resolution for classifier-specific positive labels, and retained trigger settings.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Fixed scorecard catalog naming to resolve each member from its pinned classifier revision, not the latest globally renamed classifier. Regression spec covers two scorecards pinning old and renamed revisions, deduplicated historical lookups, and no mutations. All 106 UI specs and production build pass. Read-only browser check confirms historical Anthus revision 2 retains Knowledge Bases revision 4 while active revision 3 uses Papyrus revision 5. Production definitions, labels, and runs were not changed. This is partial versioned-app acceptance, not closure of migration/runtime acceptance.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Runtime provenance integration: application trace events now explicitly carry the pinned classifier revision and scorecard definition revision/fingerprint; shared transport identifies all member revision pins. Displayed predictions carry classifier revision alongside their actual learned version fingerprint. A specs-first API-owned SQLite regression prepares a shared request, publishes a newer renamed classifier, restarts, and records explained labels/metrics: all outputs retain original definition pins and only one fake model call occurs. Existing historical events are not rewritten. Focused runtime/session/worker specs: 40 passed. Broader migration, restoration and UI acceptance remain open.
